dataset.description: Contemporary Baltic artworks referencing to themes of folklore and mythology

distribution.title:
The purpose is to identify contemporary Latvian/Baltic artworks referring to underworld mythology, allowing the categorization of works according to research objectives and the selection of artists for close-up case studies. 
The material's origins include personal archives of researchers, photos from exhibitions, scans of printed material, publicly available images on social network services, and other online sources. Part of the material will be acquired via crowdsourcing.

dmp.description:
Two datasets on the uses of chthonic folklore and mythology references in Latvian contemporary art, with few Estonian and Lithuanian examples.
1) images of artworks, including information on author, time, context, and mythological/folkloric content. Partially crowdsourced. 
2) researcher-artist interviews (including transcripts and photos) conducted with the walking ethnography method. 

The project - Contemporary Art and Folklore: Unlocking the Underworld (UNART) - is dedicated to examining the burgeoning representations of chthonic mythology within Latvian contemporary art. The project investigates how evocations of the folkloric underworld catalyze, sustain, and invigorate the dynamics of cultural and social critique in creative practices since 1991.
UNARTexplores the Latvian art scene through a multidisciplinary lens, combining textual and contextual analysis with insights from post-socialist art history, feminist aesthetics, ecocriticism, postcolonial and post-Marxist theories, and creative ethnography. This innovative approach aims to uncover new social and political dimensions of the long-standing relationship between folklore and professional arts.
The project is spearheaded by two researchers with combined expertise in folklore studies and contemporary art, supported by two doctoral candidates.
This initiative contributes a contemporary chapter to Latvian art history and provides a replicable model for comparative research and mapping emerging trends in post-socialist Europe.
